ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which list is in alphabetical order? (1 mark)
   A. sister, cousin, brother, aunt
   B. aunt, cousin, brother, sister
   C. aunt, brother, cousin, sister
   D. brother, aunt, cousin, sister

2. Why should you check your form before handing it in? (1 mark)
   A. To lose it
   B. To find missing or wrong information
   C. To make it dirty
   D. To hide it

3. What does 'Haste makes waste' mean? (1 mark)
   A. If you hurry, you may make mistakes and waste things
   B. Waste is good
   C. Food is wasted at night
   D. Hurry is always best

4. What is the plural of 'knife'? (1 mark)
   A. knives
   B. knifes
   C. knifs
   D. knifees

5. What is the plural of 'photo'? (1 mark)
   A. photoss
   B. photos
   C. photoes
   D. photees

6. Reading a text again more slowly to understand it well is called (1 mark)
   A. scanning
   B. copying
   C. silent singing
   D. intensive reading

7. In the pattern 'enough + noun + to + verb', the word after 'to' is a (1 mark)
   A. name
   B. noun
   C. adjective
   D. verb

8. A caption is (1 mark)
   A. a song
   B. a kind of camera
   C. a colour
   D. words that explain a picture

9. In which direction does the sun set? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. West
   C. North
   D. South

10. What is a good habit for a listener? (1 mark)
   A. Look away
   B. Talk while others speak
   C. Look at the speaker and do not interrupt
   D. Play with things

11. Why should you return borrowed books on time? (1 mark)
   A. To make the book dirty
   B. Because books are heavy
   C. To forget the title
   D. So others can read them too

12. Which is a good rule for a reading club? (1 mark)
   A. Listen politely and take turns
   B. Tear pages
   C. Take books home and keep them
   D. Talk all the time

13. Which words link one picture to the next? (1 mark)
   A. big, small, tall
   B. red, blue, green
   C. first, then, at last
   D. mango, rice, milk

14. Which sentence shows two actions going on at the same time in the past? (1 mark)
   A. I cooked and my sister washes plates.
   B. I have cooked while she washed.
   C. I am cooking and my sister was washing plates.
   D. I was cooking while my sister was washing plates.

15. Which helping verb completes: 'I ____ writing a letter now.'? (1 mark)
   A. is
   B. are
   C. am
   D. was

16. Which word needs a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. morning
   B. season
   C. Friday
   D. week

17. What should you do at a full stop when reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Speed up
   B. Skip the next word
   C. Shout
   D. Pause a little

18. What is the contraction of 'will not'? (1 mark)
   A. wil'nt
   B. won't
   C. willn't
   D. wont

19. What is the contraction of 'they are'? (1 mark)
   A. theyr'e
   B. they're
   C. thay're
   D. they'er

20. Which sentence is a good ending for a story? (1 mark)
   A. Farm.
   B. And the sun.
   C. We caught the goat together, and I was tired but proud.
   D. Then a goat.

21. Which simile compares using 'as ... as'? (1 mark)
   A. The maize was as tall as a door.
   B. The tall maize stood.
   C. The maize grew tall.
   D. The maize like a door.

22. Which of these can spread HIV? (1 mark)
   A. Hugging a friend
   B. Sharing a plate of food
   C. Sharing a razor blade
   D. Playing football together

23. Which sentence is a direct question and needs a question mark at the end? (1 mark)
   A. We went home
   B. I like apples
   C. Where is the school
   D. Please close the door

24. What does proofreading mean? (1 mark)
   A. Writing a new composition
   B. Checking your work for mistakes
   C. Counting the pages
   D. Reading only the title

25. Which is the correct spelling of the word for a person who is not just an acquaintance? (1 mark)
   A. frend
   B. freind
   C. friend
   D. frind

26. Which is the correct spelling of the word used to give a reason? (1 mark)
   A. because
   B. becouse
   C. becuase
   D. becase

27. Which of these helps you speak fluently? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking as fast as possible
   B. Never looking at the audience
   C. Practising what you want to say
   D. Mumbling

28. What sounds does the letter x usually make in 'box'? (1 mark)
   A. /ks/
   B. /gz/
   C. /z/
   D. /f/

29. Which word has a silent h? (1 mark)
   A. help
   B. hand
   C. honest
   D. house

30. What is a caption? (1 mark)
   A. The last paragraph
   B. The name of the newspaper
   C. A short line that explains a picture
   D. A kind of advert

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write two sentences using 'compose' and 'reply'. (2 marks)

32. Write four sentences using in, on, under and between. (4 marks)

33. Explain the proverb 'A stitch in time saves nine'. (2 marks)

34. Write the plurals of: bus, story, wolf, mouse. (2 marks)

35. List three things a child must never give to a stranger online. (3 marks)

36. Why did the teacher say the prize message might be a trick? (3 marks)

37. Write two minimal pairs for /l/ and /r/. (2 marks)

38. Give the meaning of four words from the lesson: injury, treatment, painkiller, poison. (4 marks)

39. Complete the sentences: (a) We have enough plates ___ (eat) the meal. (b) There is enough rice ___ (feed) the guests. (2 marks)

40. Give a situation in which 'Prevention is better than cure' applies. (2 marks)

41. Arrange in alphabetical order: goat, cow, hen, dog. (2 marks)

42. Explain why we say 'a university' but 'an umbrella'. (3 marks)

43. Why is it important to use polite words? Give two reasons. (4 marks)

44. Write four sentences to advise classmates on keeping the school toilets clean. (4 marks)

45. Write a polite request to borrow a ruler from a classmate. (2 marks)

46. Give three safety rules for using the internet. (4 marks)

47. Explain why flies are dangerous to health. (2 marks)

48. What kind of person is Kamau in 'The Clean-Up Day'? Give a reason from the text. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — aunt, brother, cousin, sister
   a, b, c, s is the order of the first letters.

2. B — To find missing or wrong information
   Checking finds mistakes that can cause problems later.

3. A — If you hurry, you may make mistakes and waste things
   Rushing often leads to errors.

4. A — knives
   Change fe to ves.

5. B — photos
   Photo just adds s.

6. D — intensive reading
   Intensive reading means careful, slow reading.

7. D — verb
   To is followed by a verb such as sit or eat.

8. D — words that explain a picture
   Captions tell us what a picture shows.

9. B — West
   The sun sets in the west.

10. C — Look at the speaker and do not interrupt
   Good listeners give attention.

11. D — So others can read them too
   It shows responsibility and fairness.

12. A — Listen politely and take turns
   Politeness keeps everyone included.

13. C — first, then, at last
   They are linking words for order.

14. D — I was cooking while my sister was washing plates.
   'While' links two past progressive actions.

15. C — am
   'I' takes 'am' in the present progressive.

16. C — Friday
   Days of the week begin with capital letters.

17. D — Pause a little
   A full stop tells the reader to pause.

18. B — won't
   'Will not' becomes 'won't'.

19. B — they're
   The apostrophe replaces the a in 'are'.

20. C — We caught the goat together, and I was tired but proud.
   An ending tells how the story finishes and how people felt.

21. A — The maize was as tall as a door.
   'As tall as a door' is an as ... as simile.

22. C — Sharing a razor blade
   HIV can pass through blood, so razor blades must never be shared.

23. C — Where is the school
   It is a direct question.

24. B — Checking your work for mistakes
   Proofread for spelling, capitals and punctuation.

25. C — friend
   Friend is spelt f-r-i-e-n-d.

26. A — because
   Because is spelt b-e-c-a-u-s-e.

27. C — Practising what you want to say
   Practice reduces hesitation.

28. A — /ks/
   In 'box', x says k and s together.

29. C — honest
   'Honest' is said 'onest'.

30. C — A short line that explains a picture
   A caption describes a picture.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: I will compose an email to my uncle. He will reply tomorrow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The coins are in the box. The book is on the table. The cat is under the chair. The shop is between the bank and the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fixing a small problem early stops it becoming a bigger problem that takes more work.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixing early and 1 for avoiding bigger work.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: buses, stories, wolves, mice
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name, home address, school name, password.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each, up to 3.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: It promised a prize but asked for personal details, and some people send such messages to steal information.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for prize, 1 mark for details, 1 mark for stealing.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: light, right and load, road.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Injury: harm done to the body. Treatment: care given to a sick person. Painkiller: medicine that reduces pain. Poison: something that can make you very ill or kill you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) to eat (b) to feed
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Washing hands before eating prevents illness, which is better than getting sick and needing medicine.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a situation and 1 for linking it to the proverb.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: cow, dog, goat, hen
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for c and d first, 1 mark for g and h last.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Both start with the letter u, but university starts with the consonant sound 'yoo', so it takes a. Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so it takes an. We choose by sound, not by letter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example and 1 mark for the sound rule.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Polite words show respect and make people feel welcome. They help people to cooperate and be friendly.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each reason.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands with soap after using the toilet. Do not throw rubbish in the latrine. Keep the door closed. Tell the teacher about any damage.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible sentence.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: May I borrow your ruler, please?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for may I and 1 mark for please.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use it with an adult, keep your password secret, do not give your name or address to strangers, tell an adult if something frightens you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule, up to 4.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Flies land on waste and then on food, so they carry germs to the food we eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for waste then food and 1 mark for germs spreading.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Observant and responsible: he noticed a hole in the fence and said it should be fixed at once.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality and 1 for evidence.
